metadata.description: They appear when the snow flowers bloom. When the petals fall, they retreat to places unknown again.
It senses coming disasters and appears before people only to warn them of impending danger.
Discarding its shell made it nimble. To keep itself from dehydrating, it wraps its body in bands of membrane.
Once upon a time, a king with an Aegislash reigned over the land. His Pokémon eventually drained him of life, and his kingdom fell with him.
This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.
On sunny days, it flies freely through the sky and blends into the clouds. It sings in a beautiful soprano.
Amaura is an ancient Pokémon that has gone extinct. Specimens of this species can sometimes be found frozen in ice.
To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.
Amoonguss mimics Poké Balls. It is not yet clear whether this mimicry is effective against other Pokémon.
When it gets dark, the light from its bright, shiny tail can be seen from far away on the ocean’s surface.
It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.
This Pokémon ancestor was reanimated from a fossil. It lived in the sea and hunted with its claws.
When some Lechonk come along to lick the sweet nectar on Appletun’s back, Appletun will spew sticky nectar at them to drive them away.
Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.
This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder.
It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.
Archen is said to be the ancestor of bird Pokémon. It lived in treetops, eating berries and bug Pokémon.
It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.
The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.
This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.
It attaches silk to its prey and sets it free. Later, it tracks the silk to the prey and its friends.
It went ashore after evolving. Its entire body is clad in a sturdy armor.
This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.
The scents Aromatisse can produce range from sweet smells that bolster allies to foul smells that sap an opponent’s will to fight.
It takes down prey by charging into them with its hard, pointed jaw. But Arrokuda’s eyesight is poor, so this tactic has a low success rate.
Known as Articuno, this Pokémon fires beams that can immobilize opponents as if they had been frozen solid.
This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.
When gripped by rage, Aurorus will emanate freezing air, covering everything around it in ice.
This Pokémon uses its massive icy body to flatten anything that gets in its way. When it’s floating out on the ocean, it looks exactly like drift ice.
The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.
If you see peculiar teeth marks on boulders or trees, it means an Axew is likely living nearby.
The dreaded Being of Willpower. Legends tell of this Pokémon manipulating the will of its adversaries and turning them into puppets of its own.
By keeping still and listening intently, it can tell what is in even wild, fast-moving rivers.
Its tail is packed full of the nutrients it needs to grow.
It probes muddy riverbeds with its two long whiskers. A slimy film protects its body.
It swims at speeds of over 100 knots and battles fiercely with pods of Finizen over prey.
Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui’s rivers is Basculegion’s equal.
Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.
It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.
The buds that ring its neck give off a spicy aroma that perks people up.
Feared as the Snow-White Demon in northern lands, Beartic uses its frosty claws and fangs to attack prey.
A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.
Its best attack involves flying around at high speed, striking with poison needles, then flying off.
What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.
When the heavy rainfall season ends, it is drawn out by warm sunlight to dance in the open.
It prefers hot and humid environments. It is quick at capturing prey with its vines.
Bergmite protects itself by coating its body in ice formed by frigid air of −148 degrees Fahrenheit. It fights with Frigibax whenever they meet.
The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.
The jets of water it spouts from the rocket cannons on its shell can punch through thick steel.
Flames spout from its wrists, enveloping its knuckles. Its punches scorch its foes.
Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.
The eggs it lays are filled with happiness. Eating even one bite will bring a smile to anyone.
Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.
It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.
Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.
From its eyes, it can expel excess moisture from its body. This liquid is similar in composition to human sweat.
These Pokémon live in herds of about 20 individuals. Bouffalant that betray the herd will lose the hair on their heads for some reason.
A Greedent drawn in by the sweet scent of these Pokémon will tuck the Bounsweet in among the berries in its tail and carry them all away.
When the twig is plucked from its tail, friction sets the twig alight. The flame is used to send signals to its allies.
Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.
Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.
The seeds on its tail are made of toxic spores. It knocks out foes with quick, virtually invisible punches.
It brought rains by opening portals to another world. It was revered as a bringer of plentiful harvests.
They are found in ancient tombs. The patterns on their backs are said to be imbued with mysterious power.
It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.
When the sun’s light strengthens, the bud atop this Pokémon’s head opens. This is a sign to the people that the harsh winter is over, and the season of budding has begun.
It inflates its flotation sac, keeping its face above water in order to watch for prey movement.
For some time after its birth, it grows by taking nourishment from the seed on its back.
My hypothesis as to why Buneary rolls up its ears is that its hearing is far too keen. I surmise that the Pokémon protects its hearing by limiting the sound that may enter its ears.
It’s very sensitive to danger. The sound of Corviknight’s flapping will have Bunnelby digging a hole to hide underground in moments.
It loves the nectar of flowers and can locate flower patches that have even tiny amounts of pollen.
It lives in arid locations. Its yellow flowers bloom once a year.
It lives in deserts. It becomes active at night when it hunts for prey exhausted from the desert’s heat.
Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.
Traditional Paldean dishes can be extremely spicy because they include the shed front teeth of Capsakid among their ingredients.
Due to the coal tar created inside it, the heap of coal on Carkol’s back never falls apart, even when the Pokémon rolls around at high speeds.
Though this is a plant Pokémon, it has a gluttonous and unruly temperament. Carnivine attacks its prey with its cavernous maw wide open.
This Pokémon emerges from the water in search of prey despite the fact that it moves more slowly on land.
The silk coating its body is thin but sufficiently strong. Cascoon’s silk has a luster and texture superior to that of Silcoon’s, and clothes made using Cascoon silk are regarded as top-notch.
Its appearance changes with the weather. Recently, its molecules were found to be just like water.
This is Castform’s form when pelted by rain. In an experiment where it was placed in a shower, this Pokémon didn’t change to this form.
This is Castform’s form when caught in a hailstorm. Its whole body is chilled, and its skin is partially frozen!
Castform changes to this form when it basks in bright sunlight. When you touch its glowing skin, it feels all dried out!
It releases a stench from its red antennae to repel enemies. It grows by molting repeatedly.
It has the power to travel across time, but it is said to appear only in peaceful times.
While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.
An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.
Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.
It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice.
In homes illuminated by Chandelure instead of lights, funerals were a constant occurrence— or so it’s said.
It walks carefully to prevent its egg from breaking. However, it is extremely fast at running away.
Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.
It is said that Charizard’s fire burns hotter if it has experienced harsh battles.
The fire on the tip of its tail is a measure of its life. If the Pokémon is healthy, its tail burns intensely.
In the rocky mountains where Charmeleon live, their fiery tails shine at night like stars.
A versatile performer skilled in the imitation of human speech. It is said that older, more experienced Chatot can even understand the meaning of the words they mimic.
Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim’s folded petals.
Once the fruit growing alongside the main body is large and plump, Cherubi will use the nutrients within to evolve. The fruit then detaches, becoming nourishment for other creatures.
When it takes a defensive posture with its fists guarding its face, it could withstand a bomb blast.
Such a thick shell of wood covers its head and back that even a direct hit from a truck wouldn’t faze it.
A popular game among children is to lift up sticks that Chewtle have bitten onto to see whose Chewtle can hang on the longest.
The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.
The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.
It uses the leaf on its head to determine the air’s temperature and humidity. It loves to sunbathe.
Full of vigor and always in high spirits. It was once known by the name “Lantern-Tail” and feared as some kind of apparition.
Can emit waves of air powerful enough to knock out prey taller than itself. I hypothesize that it amplifies the faint sound of wind within its body.
It discharges positive and negative electricity from the tips of its antennae to shock its foes.
This Pokémon gave me an excruciating headache when it seemingly cried out without making a sound. Perhaps there are some sounds that the human ear is simply incapable of hearing.
A special oil that seeps through their fur helps them avoid attacks. The oil fetches a high price at market.
It’s skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.
It makes a single pearl during its lifetime. The pearl is said to amplify psychic power.
An ancient clay figurine was exposed to a mysterious ray of light, and it came to life as a Pokémon.
Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon’s night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.
In silhouette, they resemble twinkling starlight. When shooting stars rain from the night sky, Cleffa gather in numbers and dance as though they are indeed incarnations of the stars.
Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn’t alarmed when that happens—it knows they’ll grow back. It’s about as smart as a three-year-old.
It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.
It’s gentle usually but fearsome when angered. With a body that burns at over 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit, it crushes foes and turns them to ash.
From the moment it’s born, this Pokémon radiates the air of a leader. Its presence will calm even vicious foes.
The trio is together from birth. It constantly gathers nectar from flowers to please Vespiquen.
Its kicking mastery lets it loose 10 kicks per second. It emits sharp cries to intimidate foes.
These Pokémon smell very nice. All Comfey wear different flowers, so each of these Pokémon has its own individual scent.
When going all out, this Pokémon throws aside its concrete pillars and leaps at opponents to pummel them with its fists.
Copperajah are prideful, cantankerous Pokémon. Specimens with vibrant green skin command the respect of others of their kind.
Many live in the clean seas of the south. They apparently can’t live in polluted waters.
Sudden climate change wiped out this ancient kind of Corsola. This Pokémon absorbs others’ life-force through its branches.
Although its wings have partly turned to steel and become heavy as a result, this Pokémon flies through the skies with ease.
This intelligent Pokémon will quickly learn how to use any tool it can hold in its beak or its talons.
It sucks in dust from the air at an astounding rate, frantically building up energy within its core as preparation for evolution.
Cosmog is very curious but not very cautious, often placing itself in danger. If things start to look dicey, it teleports away.
Weaving together the cotton of both Cottonee and Eldegoss produces exquisite cloth that’s highly prized by many luxury brands.
Though its punches are powerful, this Pokémon’s movements are sluggish. It blows icy bubbles from its mouth to immobilize its opponents.
If it loses its pincers, they’ll quickly regrow. The pincers are popular ingredients in paella since their shells produce a tasty soup stock.
It lives in the shallows of warm seas. When the tide goes out, it digs up prey from beaches.
This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.
The half-swallowed Pikachu is so startled that it isn’t struggling yet, but it’s still looking for a chance to strike back.
The slightest shock is sometimes enough to get this Pokémon to spit out the Arrokuda lodged in its throat.
An incredibly rare sight. They duel each other by ramming their heads together, and the resulting sound echoes throughout the area like the pealing of a bell.
Cresselia is reminiscent of the crescent moon. It leaves a brilliant line of light in its wake as it flies across the night sky. I daresay it resembles the heavenly maiden who created the Milky Way.
It rarely fights fairly, but that is strictly to ensure survival. It is popular as a mascot.
The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.
When Cubchoo starts sneezing, watch out! If it spatters you with its frosty snot, you’ll get frostbite.
Cufant can lift loads weighing five tons. In the mornings, it heads into caves with its herd, in search of the ore on which these Pokémon feed.
Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.
An opponent’s aura can tell Cutiefly what that opponent’s next move will be. Then Cutiefly can glide around the attack and strike back.
It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.
The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma.
Though it has a gentle disposition, it’s also very strong. It will quickly freeze the snowball on its head before going for a headbutt.
Darmanitan takes this form when enraged. It won’t stop spewing flames until its rage has settled, even if its body starts to melt.
When wounded, it stops moving. It goes as still as stone to meditate, sharpening its mind and spirit.
Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.
The colder they get, the more energetic they are. They freeze their breath to make snowballs, using them as ammo for playful snowball fights.
In a tenth of a second, it can nock and fire an arrow quill, piercing an opponent’s weak point before they notice what’s happening.
The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye’s feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui’s extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.
Dedenne emit electrical waves from the whiskers on their cheeks to communicate with each other. When low on electricity, they curl up and sleep.
The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.
It is highly popular among Trainers for its sublime fur. It does not keep a nest.
It always carries its food with it, wherever it goes. If attacked, it throws its food at the opponent.
Using psychic power, it generates a fiery vortex of 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit, incinerating foes swept into this whirl of flame.

metadata.description: An alien virus that fell to earth on a meteorite underwent a DNA mutation to become this Pokémon.
In snow, the pure white coat covering its body obscures it from predators.
Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.
After lowering its anchor, it waits for its prey. It catches large Wailord and drains their life-force.
The fur on its belly retains heat exceptionally well. People used to make heavy winter clothing from fur shed by this Pokémon.
Its skin is very thin. If it is exposed to light, its blood heats up, causing it to grow weak.
Its three hairs change shape depending on Diglett’s mood. They’re a useful communication tool among these Pokémon.

The head and tail appear to belong to two separate creatures; both help each other out from within their shared apple. Dipplin coat their apples with syrup produced within their bodies. The layers of fragrant syrup beguile opponents.​
It can freely recombine its own cellular structure to transform into other life-forms.
When Doduo evolves into this odd breed, one of its heads splits into two. This Pokémon runs at nearly 40 mph.
The brains in its two heads appear to communicate emotions to each other with a telepathic power.
It basks in the sun to its heart’s content until the fruits on its head ripen. After that, Dolliv departs from human settlements and goes on a journey.
It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.
Donphan is normally a calm Pokémon, but once it is enraged, it will curl its body into a ball and charge at you while rolling.
As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.
Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.
The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.
The fastest Dragapult of the group is always surrounded by Dreepy that want to fly at sonic speed.
It is called the divine Pokémon. When its entire body brightens slightly, the weather changes.
This Pokémon stores up energy in its lungs, then shoots it out. It takes care of Dreepy and battles alongside them until they’re all grown up.
It is born large to start with. It repeatedly sheds its skin as it steadily grows longer.
Drednaw lurks along the shoreline. When prey come to drink water, Drednaw stretches its neck out and chomps down on them.
It has a habit of biting at Clauncher even though it doesn’t feed on them. This is said to be vestigial behavior from when Dreepy was alive.
They carry people and Pokémon, but the wind can catch them, so there can’t be a fixed destination.
Because of the way it floats aimlessly, an old folktale calls it a “signpost for wandering spirits.”
Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it keeps enemies out of its territory by laying traps everywhere.
Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.
They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.
It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.
A recent study uncovered that the number of segments a Dudunsparce’s body has is determined by the Pokémon’s genes.
The three of them get along very well. Through their formidable teamwork, they defeat powerful opponents.
If spotted, it escapes by burrowing with its tail. It can float just slightly using its wings.
Its brain has split into two, and the two halves rarely think alike. Its actions are utterly unpredictable.
The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.
With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.
Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.
Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element stones.
It can evolve into a variety of forms. Eevee's genes are the key to solving the mysteries of Pokémon evolution.
If you lick the ice covering its face, you’ll find it has a faintly salty taste. This species rode here on ocean currents from a cold, faraway land.
If you lick the ice covering its face, you’ll find it has a faintly salty taste. This species rode here on ocean currents from a cold, faraway land.
The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.
Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.
Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.
Using electricity stored in its fur, it stimulates its muscles to heighten its reaction speed.
It explodes in response to even minor stimuli. It is feared, with the nickname of the Bomb Ball.
The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
They generate electricity by spinning their arms. During a thunderstorm, if one hears the lively voices of children out in the wilderness, what one is actually hearing are the voices of Elekid.
It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.
This Pokémon absolutely loves sweet berries. Sometimes it stuffs its cheeks full of so much food that it can’t fly properly.
Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.
When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon’s love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.
It is said that when it roars, a volcano erupts somewhere around the globe.
It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.
It uses the fine hair that covers its body to sense air currents and predict its enemy’s actions.
There’s enough psychic power in Espurr to send a wrestler flying, but because this power can’t be controlled, Espurr finds it troublesome.
It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.
Its six eggs converse using telepathy. They can quickly gather if they become separated.
It is called the Walking Jungle. If a head grows too big, it falls off and becomes an Exeggcute.
This Pokémon’s psychic powers aren’t as strong as they once were. The head on this Exeggutor’s tail scans surrounding areas with weak telepathy.
Its howls can be heard over six miles away. It emits all sorts of noises from the ports on its body.
The leader, known as the brass, uses its extendible horn to issue orders to the others when it’s time to change formation.
It can’t live without the stalk it holds. That’s why it defends the stalk from attackers with its life.
The stalks of leeks are thicker and longer in the Galar region. Farfetch’d that adapted to these stalks took on a unique form.
The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.
As it walks, it munches on a twig in place of a snack. It intimidates opponents by puffing hot air out of its ears.
Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.
The yeast in Fidough’s breath is useful for cooking, so this Pokémon has been protected by people since long ago.
Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.
Because of its rubbery, electricity-resistant skin, it can store lots of electricity in its fur.
Flabébé wears a crown made from pollen it’s collected from its flower. The crown has hidden healing properties.
Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.
It uses its own body fluid to repair its apple. Strong Flapple that have won many battles have apples that are clay colored all over.
Its territory has a radius of just over a mile. If any bird Pokémon should enter, it will show them no mercy.
Fletchling can be found in both rural and urban areas. They once had a huge territorial dispute with Squawkabilly. Fights broke out all over town.
It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge.
It is a common sight around fishing ports. It is known to rescue people and help fishers carry what they caught.
It gives its own power to flowers, pouring its heart into caring for them. Floette never forgives anyone who messes up a flower bed.
The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.
Its life can span several hundred years. It’s said to devote its entire life to protecting gardens.
It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.
It whips up sandstorms with powerful flaps of its wings. It is known as the Desert Spirit.
Many Trainers give their Fomantis their own flowerpots so they can sunbathe in peace and quiet.
This Pokémon prefers damp places. It spurts out poison spores to repel approaching enemies.
Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.
Fraxure uses its thick tusks to neatly cut prey into two portions—one to eat now and one to save for later.
This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.
It protects its skin by covering its body in delicate bubbles. Beneath its happy-go-lucky air, it keeps a watchful eye on its surroundings.
Its swiftness is unparalleled. It can scale a tower of more than 2,000 feet in a minute’s time.
It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.
It causes blizzards as it flies around with its huge, chill-emanating wings. Clean meltwater is its favorite thing to drink.
Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.
Left alone, its fur will grow longer and longer, but it will only allow someone it trusts to cut it.
It loves sparkly things. It seeks treasures in caves and hoards the loot in its nest.
Because it can sense what its foe is thinking, its attacks burst out first, fast, and fierce.
The protuberances on its head serve as sensors. It can even detect distant prey.
It unleashes psychokinetic energy at full power when protecting a Trainer it has bonded closely with.
Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt.
It appears on beaches where the waters are shallow. Once it catches prey, it will slowly melt them with its mucus before slurping them up.
It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.
It nests in horizontal holes warmed by geothermal heat. Foes who get too close can expect to be pounced on and bitten.
It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.
It wanders around, carrying an old coin on its back. It survives by draining the life-force from humans who try to pick up its coin.
Girafarig’s tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.
It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.
Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.
Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.

Its tail is tipped by a thick, horrible stinger. To bring down prey, it will first obscure their vision by covering their faces with its body, and then it will use the stinger to inject them with venom.
Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.
Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.
The nectar it drools from its mouth smells so atrocious that it can make noses curl from more than a mile away.
These Pokémon live in herds in mountainous places. The victor in their contests of clashing horns will become the leader of the herd.
It swims gracefully along on the quiet, slow-moving rivers and lakes of which it is so fond.
This Pokémon is uncontrollable when enraged. It rampages on and on, lashing its tail with enough power to send a dump truck flying.
Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.
Goomy’s horns are excellent sensory organs that cover all five of Goomy’s senses. Goomy picks up on danger from the movement of the air.
It lives at the bottom of the sea. In the springtime, its pink body turns more vivid for some reason.

A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.
Born when around 10% of Zygarde’s cells have been gathered from all over, this form is skilled in close-range combat.

The Zygarde Cells form the rest of Zygarde's body and are only able to act on the Core's orders. The Zygarde Cells allows the Zygarde Core to observe the ecosystem, allowing them to see through their eyes.
Born when all of Zygarde’s cells have been gathered together, it uses force to neutralize those who harm the ecosystem.

metadata.description: The Zygarde Core remains in watch of the region, usually living in caves. The Cores have their own will and are sometimes able to act on their own. The Zygarde Core can order Zygarde Cells, commanding them to fly towards it to form Zygarde's body in order to protect the ecosystem.
